Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Having given up attachment to results, always content and self-reliant, a liberated person does not engage in binding action even while performing all kinds of tasks.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Emotional dependence on external achievements, security, and praise.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'tyaktva karma-phalasangam nitya-trpto nirasrayah, karmany abhipravrtto 'pi naiva kincit karoti sah' (Having abandoned attachment to results, ever satisfied and independent, one does nothing binding even while fully engaged in work).
Outcome/Resolution: Instills deep inner autonomy and contentment, protecting the individual from emotional volatility caused by external events.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Emotional Independence: Relying on internal stability rather than external validation
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Self-Contentment: Experiencing ongoing satisfaction regardless of external conditions
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Detached Execution: Performing duties thoroughly without clinging to specific outcomes

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Tyaktva karma-phalasangam (Relinquishing attachment to the fruits of action)
Nirasrayah (Independent / without dependence on external shelter)
Naiva kincit karoti sah (Does not perform binding action)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Relinquishing attachment to results grounds the soul in eternal satisfaction, rendering all daily activities completely free from karmic reaction.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Cultivating internal self-reliance ensures that your emotional balance remains intact, no matter how chaotic or demanding your work environment becomes.
